title: With independent plot sampling, TransPlant cover exceeded species control intervals, but occurrence evidence was sensitive
abstract: A community can leave the line between cold-site and warm-site controls even when each species moves between its own two control values. We developed a held-out-plot test of this wider species-specific interval restriction. We used 40 contrasts in 20 TransPlant gradients. Species weights were selected on training plots. Independent test plots supplied a product statistic with a sampling-variance correction. Cover gave positive secondary scores, including a test without relative-cover closure. The primary occurrence result was near zero at its lower uncertainty limit and was sensitive to gradient selection. It did not give robust evidence across checks. The method needs independent plots and group means. Soil transport, changed moisture, disturbance, past control states and measurement error can also cause departures. The results do not identify a cause or reject general lag models with changing targets. Source records remain external. Code, proof, aggregate results, a figure and retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Held-out tests of species values beyond current control intervals. Points show first and last census scores. Bars show 95% gradient bootstrap limits. The lower panel shows last-census occurrence scores by gradient. Scores have different response scales and are not thermal tracking fractions.
